arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Elizabeth Prelogar argued that Congress enacted the law to address domestic violence in Indian Country.
Mr. Babcock argued that the right to counsel is fundamental and essential in the country.
Chief Justice Roberts asked if convictions in a tribal court count as predicates without the Indian Civil Rights Act.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the scope of federal sentencing laws. It asks if tribal court records qualify as prior convictions. The answer shapes how federal judges calculate sentences for defendants with tribal histories.

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on April 19, 2016.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The government wants the Court to allow tribal court records to count as prior offenses.
The defendant wants the Court to bar the use of tribal court records for sentencing enhancements.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The government argues that Congress intended to include all prior convictions in sentencing calculations.
The defendant argues that tribal court records lack the procedural safeguards required for federal sentencing.
